prompt: With the setting at zero, the model gives the same answer every time.
tells: gives the same answer every time
why: Low temperature makes the model pick the most likely words, so answers barely change. That's the temperature setting.
trap: Next-word prediction is always happening; the setting controls how much randomness goes in.

prompt: For brainstorming slogans, the team turns up the randomness setting to get more varied ideas.
why: Higher temperature lets less likely words through, giving more variety. Good for brainstorming.
trap: They didn't change the wording; they changed a setting.

prompt: At a very high setting, answers drift into nonsense and odd word choices.
why: Too much randomness lets unlikely words win and the text falls apart. That's temperature set too high.
trap: Nonsense isn't the same as a confident false fact; the cause is the setting.

prompt: For pulling invoice totals into a form, the developer sets temperature low so results are consistent.
why: Extraction needs the same answer each time, so randomness is turned down. That's temperature.
trap: Grounding gives the source; temperature controls how predictable the reading of it is.

prompt: Pressing regenerate gives a noticeably different story each time.
tells: a noticeably different story each time
why: Some randomness in picking words means each run can differ. That comes from the temperature setting.
trap: It does predict word by word, but the variety comes from randomness.

prompt: The writer says the poems feel predictable, so the developer raises temperature rather than changing the prompt.
tells: raises temperature rather than changing the prompt
why: Raising temperature adds variety to word choice. The fix was the randomness dial, not the wording.
trap: Prompt wording was explicitly not what changed.
